title: Insertion tabs: Positive-ink invoice
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: The input contains two rows: a sorted drawer and query values. For each query, produce the first index whose drawer value is at least that query; use the drawer's length if no such index exists. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.
descriptionMd:
The archive needs insertion tabs for new labels without disturbing an existing sorted drawer. Ivo prepares an invoice that accepts only positive ink adjustments. Zero and negative derived readings stay off the invoice.

The input contains two rows: a sorted drawer and query values. For each query, produce the first index whose drawer value is at least that query; use the drawer's length if no such index exists.

Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.

Implement insertionTabsPositiveInkInvoice(drawers, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The input has exactly two rows, each containing at most 64 integers.

Target time O(q log(n+1)); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
